observations.finding: Original nursery return, seeds in chai, squirrel damage to carrot bed, Dorito ears, gnome assault and flailing rescue, hose combat, tomato/spinach planting, lime sapling, trellis, and sunset bench remain in original causal order. Heather-only historical household is preserved. No meaningful alternative exists in this story or its comparison record.

Buddy liking the nursery because it asked nothing of him establishes his comfort motive. Heather's lunch-in-breakfast response is specific to the seed accident. Neet's concern about the smiling gnome and his temporary hose victory express disproportionate earnestness without constant shouting. Buddy's pot-with-a-face line and avoidance of the remaining pots supply dry restraint.

Buddy abandons chosen shade to chase the squirrel, causes soil damage, prepares a second attempt, notices the untouched row, deliberately stops, and chooses the longer safe route. His later dry shade is a small earned success. He does more than comment on Neet.

The three images offer different beats: simultaneous material aftermath, an opponent's infuriating immobility, and false victory. Their pauses fit paragraph boundaries without splitting attribution; each action resumes afterward. Bare beds prevent implausible immediate germination; the attack precedes the final chipped-gnome reference.

Heather finishes the garden and relocates her cup, a practical callback. Sunset slowing and Buddy resting on her lap remain warm; gently returning Neet's paw to the bench closes his unfinished gnome vigilance without a forced final wisecrack. Leaving this ending unillustrated avoids crowding it.
